newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mixed Australian stocks crawl just higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Australian stocks crawl just higher at open.

text.p: The Australian share market was little changed at the open on Thursday after mixed finishes on offshore markets failed to provide any inspiration to local investors.
The All Ordinaries index added 2.2 points to 2,391.4 at the start.
Most of the leaders managed only several cents movement either way, with banks the most active in an otherwise slow start.
"We are not expecting too much today," said a Sydney-based broker, adding that banks were likely to remain the focus after Wednesday's release of the Wallis report into the financial system.
"Some of the banks may be a bit firm again if overseas investors start looking at them."
The big banks were generally firmer in initial trade but early impetus was quickly lost and the sector turned mixed with the rest of the market.
Sector leader National Australia Bank firmed early but ran into sellers after its rapid rise on Wednesday. Its shares were 11 cents lower at A$16.00 (US$12.56).

Commonwealth Bank of Australia held narrow gains, up three cents at A$13.01 while Wednesday's big losers, ANZ Bank and Westpac Banking Corporation were both four cents lower at A$7.85 and A$6.63 respectively.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to eight, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
